items.title: [Model] Add PP-DocLayoutV4 Model Support
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48387&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48387) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48387&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48387)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This PR adds **PP-DocLayoutV4**, an end-to-end document layout analysis model that
predicts, in a single forward pass, the class of each layout element, the
quadrilateral enclosing it, and the reading order of the elements.

It follows up on #43098, which added PP-DocLayoutV3. The new model is implemented
with `modular_pp_doclayout_v4.py` on top of `pp_doclayout_v3` and `rt_detr`, so the
diff mostly reuses existing components (1180 LoC modular → 2051 LoC generated).

## What changes relative to PP-DocLayoutV3

PP-DocLayoutV4 keeps the RT-DETR skeleton (HGNetV2 backbone, AIFI hybrid encoder,
deformable decoder) and changes three things:

- **Quadrilaterals instead of masks.** V3 predicted a segmentation mask per query
  and fitted a polygon to it. V4 drops the mask branch and directly regresses a
  four-point quad in sigmoid space, which handles skewed and perspective-distorted
  documents without a mask head. The stride-4 backbone feature is no longer needed.
- **Untied per-layer heads.** Every decoder layer owns its own box and
  classification head instead of sharing one with the encoder.
- **Two reading-order heads plus a fusion step.** Alongside V3's relative-order
  head there is a successor head (ROOR). `PPDocLayoutV4S2RFusion` folds a damped
  transitive closure of the successor matrix back into the relative-order logits.

Reading order is decoded in the image processor, not in the model:
`post_process_object_detection` thresholds the successor matrix into a DAG, breaks
cycles, sorts each connected component topologically, and orders components by
their relative-order votes.

The model is inference-only in Transformers; passing `labels` raises a `ValueError`.

## Checkpoint

`PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV4_safetensors`.

⚠️ The repository is **private until the official PP-DocLayoutV4 release**, so the
usage examples and the integration test are not runnable by reviewers yet. It will
be made public at release time and I will ping reviewers so they can verify. The
non-slow tests do not touch the Hub and pass on CI.

## Parity with the reference implementation

Verified against the PaddleX layout-analysis pipeline on five images, with PaddleX's
application-level policies (`filter_overlap_boxes`, `layout_nms`,
`skip_order_labels`, `layout_unclip_ratio`, `layout_merge_bboxes_mode`) disabled —
those are deliberately left to the caller and are documented in the model card.

End to end, each side with its own preprocessing: identical detections, labels and
reading order agree exactly, scores to 6e-3, quad corners to 0.31 px (0.14 px on the
three images that are actual document scans). Feeding both sides the same `cv2`
preprocessed tensor isolates the model: 1e-6 on scores, 5e-4 px on corners, 1e-4 on
the raw order logits — so preprocessing accounts for nearly all of the end-to-end
residual.

One preprocessing detail worth calling out: rescaling to `[0, 1]` happens *before*
resizing, and the bicubic overshoot is clipped. Resizing in `uint8` rounds twice with
slightly different kernel weights and drifts far enough to permute the predicted
reading order.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/models/pp_doclayout_v4/` → 120 passed, 126 skipped, 4854 subtests
  passed (the skips are the slow/integration tests).
- `make check-repo` → all 25 checks pass.

## Before submitting
- [ ] This PR fixes a typo or improves the docs (you can dismiss the other checks if that's the case).
- [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/contributing) and the
      [Pull Request](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_checks) checks?
- [ ] Was this discussed/approved via a Github issue or the [forum](https://discuss.huggingface.co/)? Please add a link
      to it if that's the case.
- [x] Did you make sure to update the documentation with your changes according to the [guidelines](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/docs)?
- [x] Did you write any new necessary [tests](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/testing)?

## Who can review?

@molbap @vasqu — you reviewed and merged the PP-DocLayoutV3 PR (#43098), so this

items.title: Add native TR-HASH model support
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48194&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48194) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48194&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48194)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Adds native Transformers support for the TR-HASH deterministic token-routed MoE architecture and the public `AETHORIA-AI/TR-HASH-MoE-200M-160B-SFT` checkpoint.

TR-HASH differs from learned-router MoEs in three important ways:

- expert selection is a deterministic function of token IDs, layer index, and persisted multi-hash route tables;
- each token activates two of four stored experts plus an always-on shared SwiGLU branch;
- routed gate/up/down weights are stored as stacked 3D parameters.

This PR adds:

- `TRHashConfig`, `TRHashModel`, and `TRHashForCausalLM`;
- `AutoConfig`, `AutoModel`, and `AutoModelForCausalLM` mappings;
- eager and SDPA attention through the standard Transformers attention interface;
- dynamic-cache generation, gradient checkpointing, tied embeddings, persisted routing metadata, and standard save/load support;
- model documentation and a slow public-checkpoint integration test.

`inputs_embeds`-only generation is intentionally unsupported because deterministic expert routing requires the original token IDs.

## Validation

- Model suite: **134 passed, 169 skipped, 727 subtests passed**.
- Repository checks: `check_repo`, `check_auto`, `check_inits`, `check_doc_toc`, `check_config_attributes`, `check_config_docstrings`, `check_modeling_structure`, `check_modeling_rules_doc`, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The public 290-tensor checkpoint loads strictly with no missing or unexpected keys.
- Fixed-prompt SDPA logits match the reference Complexity Framework implementation exactly (`max_abs_error = 0.0`).
- Multi-token cache continuation stays within `2.58e-05` maximum absolute error and produces identical argmax tokens.

We are the model authors and can provide additional routing traces or reference logits if useful during review.

Closes #48193

items.title: Add support for Lumma Model
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47929&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47929) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47929&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47929)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## PR Overview

This PR adds native support for the Lumma AI model to the transformers library, allowing users to load and run Lumma through the standard `from_pretrained(...)` API without requiring custom remote code.

Lumma by FrontiersMind is a Llama-style decoder with efficiency-oriented architectural choices - factorized embeddings, GQA, optional layer sharing, shared KV attention, and configurable Q/QK normalization.

### Architecture
  - Factorized embeddings to reduce the size of the embedding layers.
  - Grouped Query Attention (GQA) for more efficient attention.
  - Shared KV attention, where the value projection is reused from the key projection.
  - Q-norm / QK-norm support for normalizing queries and keys.
  - Optional layer sharing, allowing the same layers to be reused multiple times.
  - RoPE and Llama-style MLP, keeping the familiar Llama architecture.
 
 @Rocketknight1 @vasqu @ArthurZucker @xenova @zucchini-nlp 🤗
I would really appreciate it if you could take a look at this PR and share any feedback or suggestions. We’re hoping to get this merged soon, so please let me know if there’s anything that needs to be addressed before merging. We’ll be happy to make the necessary changes promptly.

items.title: Add dots3-note Preview model support
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47844&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47844) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47844&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47844)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This PR is submitted by the official Dots-Studio team.

This PR adds native Transformers support for **Dots 3 Note Preview**, an inference-only mixture-of-experts multimodal causal language model supporting text, image, video, and audio inputs.

The implementation follows the modular Transformers workflow and includes the model configuration, processor, image processor, audio feature extractor, modeling implementation, auto-class registrations, documentation, conversion utilities, and model tests required for native integration.

The implementation includes:

- text, image, video, and audio input processing;
- greedy multimodal generation;
- sliding-window attention and DSA indexer inference;
- multimodal cache handling during generation;
- variable-length left-padded batching;
- BF16 checkpoint support;
- fine-grained FP8 checkpoint support using dynamic activations, E4M3 weights, and a `128 x 128` weight block size;
- FP32 routing for the vision MoE router.

This integration currently targets inference. Training-specific features such as gradient checkpointing are outside the scope of this PR.

No additional runtime dependency is introduced by this integration.

## Validation

The following checks were run against the implementation in this PR:

- the complete `tests/models/dots3_note` test directory;
- modular-to-generated modeling conversion and synchronization checks;
- Ruff formatting and lint checks;
- repository diff checks;
- clean loading of the real BF16 and FP8 checkpoints;
- greedy end-to-end generation through `AutoModelForMultimodalLM`;
- text reasoning tests, including GSM8K-style problems;
- speech transcription;
- image question answering;
- video understanding;
- multimodal cache and masking regression tests;
- FP8 dequantization with non-divisible weight dimensions;
- DSA projection precision and derived-weight cache invalidation;
- vision MoE near-tie routing precision.

Both the BF16 and FP8 checkpoints passed the end-to-end text, image, video, and audio validation cases with finite outputs and successful greedy generation.

The corresponding public checkpoint links and finalized model organization metadata will be added after this PR is  merged.

## Code Agent Policy

The Transformers repo is currently being overwhelmed by a large number of PRs and issue comments written by
code agents. These often are low-quality, or fix extremely minor issues that occur rarely or never in practice.
As a result, we're instituting a rule that **first-time contributors should not use code agents to submit PRs or issues**.
We'd also ask autonomous "OpenClaw"-like agents not to open any PRs or issues.

Issues/PRs from first-time contributors that violate this rule will probably just be closed without review, and we
might block you, especially if you open more than one or appear to be deliberately ignoring this. We especially do not
want new contributors to jump in on random issues to contribute an agent-written fix. This creates lots of noise
for reviewers and other users and will almost certainly get you blocked.

For more information, please read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] (First-time contributors only): I confirm that this PR description and code is not written by an LLM or code agent

items.title: Add support for Quatfit1 multimodal models
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47081)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47081)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# Add native support for the Quatfit1 multimodal architecture

## Summary

This pull request adds native support for **Quatfit1**, a multimodal architecture derived from Gemma4, to the Transformers library.

Quatfit1 introduces a dedicated `model_type` (`quatfit1`) while leveraging the existing Gemma4 implementation. Native integration allows Quatfit models to be loaded directly through the Transformers Auto Classes without requiring `trust_remote_code=True`.

---

## Motivation

Currently, Quatfit models require remote code execution to be loaded:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
```

With native Transformers support, users can simply write:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini"
)
```

---

## Features

Quatfit1 supports:

- Text generation
- Image understanding
- Audio understanding
- Video understanding
- Multimodal instruction following
- Long-context inference
- Hugging Face Auto Classes

---

## Architecture

Quatfit1 is implemented as a Gemma4-derived architecture with full configuration, modeling, feature extraction, image processing, video processing, and processor classes.

The following configuration classes are introduced:

- `Quatfit1Config` (`model_type = "quatfit1"`)
- `Quatfit1TextConfig` (`model_type = "quatfit1_text"`)
- `Quatfit1VisionConfig` (`model_type = "quatfit1_vision"`)
- `Quatfit1AudioConfig` (`model_type = "quatfit1_audio"`)

The following model classes are introduced:

- `Quatfit1ForConditionalGeneration`
- `Quatfit1ForCausalLM`
- `Quatfit1Model`
- `Quatfit1TextModel`
- `Quatfit1VisionModel`
- `Quatfit1AudioModel`
- `Quatfit1PreTrainedModel`

The following processing classes are introduced:

- `Quatfit1Processor`
- `Quatfit1AudioFeatureExtractor`
- `Quatfit1ImageProcessor`
- `Quatfit1ImageProcessorPil`
- `Quatfit1VideoProcessor`

A weight conversion script is also included:

- `convert_quatfit1_weights.py`

---

## Files Added

```
src/transformers/models/quatfit1/
__init__.py
configuration_quatfit1.py
convert_quatfit1_weights.py
feature_extraction_quatfit1.py
image_processing_quatfit1.py
image_processing_pil_quatfit1.py
modeling_quatfit1.py
modular_quatfit1.py
processing_quatfit1.py
video_processing_quatfit1.py
```

---

## Auto Class Support

This PR registers Quatfit1 for:

- `AutoConfig` -- via `Quatfit1Config`
- `AutoModel` -- via `Quatfit1ForConditionalGeneration`
- `AutoModelForCausalLM` -- via `Quatfit1ForConditionalGeneration`
- `AutoModelForImageTextToText` -- via `Quatfit1ForConditionalGeneration`

Auto-mappings are also registered for the audio feature extractor, image processors, video processor, and processor.

---

## Example Usage

### Text

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")
```

### Multimodal

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForImageTextToText

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")
```

---

## Backward Compatibility

This PR introduces a new architecture without modifying the behavior of existing Gemma4 models. Existing Gemma4 checkpoints continue to function as before.

---

## Test Files

```
tests/models/quatfit1/
__init__.py
test_feature_extraction_quatfit1.py
test_image_processing_quatfit1.py
test_modeling_quatfit1.py
test_processing_quatfit1.py
```

## Documentation

```
docs/source/en/model_doc/quatfit1.md
```

Added to `docs/source/en/_toctree.yml` and registered in auto-mappings.

---

## CI Status

All `make check-repository-consistency` checks pass:

- [x] Generate auto mappings (`check_auto.py`)
- [x] Public imports (`from transformers import *`)
- [x] Import complexity
- [x] Copied code consistency (`check_copies.py`)
- [x] Modular file conversions (`check_modular_conversion.py`)
- [x] Documentation table of contents
- [x] Modeling rules documentation
- [x] Docstring formatting (`check_docstrings.py`)

items.title: Add support for Quatfit1 multimodal models
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47080)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47080)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# Add native support for the Quatfit1 multimodal architecture

## Summary

This pull request adds native support for **Quatfit1**, a multimodal architecture derived from Gemma4, to the Transformers library.

Quatfit1 introduces a dedicated `model_type` (`quatfit1`) while leveraging the existing Gemma4 implementation. Native integration allows Quatfit models to be loaded directly through the Transformers Auto Classes without requiring `trust_remote_code=True`.

---

## Motivation

Currently, Quatfit models require remote code execution to be loaded:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
```

With native Transformers support, users can simply write:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini"
)
```

This improves interoperability with the Hugging Face ecosystem and provides a more seamless user experience.

---

## Features

Quatfit1 supports:

- Text generation
- Image understanding
- Audio understanding
- Video understanding
- Multimodal instruction following
- Long-context inference
- Hugging Face Auto Classes

---

## Architecture

Quatfit1 is implemented as a Gemma4-derived architecture with its own configuration classes.

The following classes are introduced:

- `Quatfit1Config`
- `Quatfit1TextConfig`
- `Quatfit1VisionConfig`
- `Quatfit1AudioConfig`
- `Quatfit1ForConditionalGeneration`

The architecture defines:

```python
model_type = "quatfit1"
```

while remaining compatible with the existing Gemma4 tokenizer and processor.

---

## Files Added

```
src/transformers/models/quatfit1/
├── __init__.py
├── configuration_quatfit1.py
└── modeling_quatfit1.py
```

---

## Auto Class Support

This PR registers Quatfit1 for:

- `AutoConfig`
- `AutoModel`
- `AutoModelForCausalLM`
- `AutoModelForImageTextToText`

allowing native loading through the Transformers Auto Classes.

---

## Example Usage

### Text

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini"
)
```

### Multimodal

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini")

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini"
)
```

---

## Compatibility

Quatfit1 is compatible with:

- Hugging Face Hub
- AutoConfig
- AutoModel
- AutoModelForCausalLM
- AutoModelForImageTextToText
- Accelerate
- Safetensors
- Device Mapping
- Generation API

---

## Backward Compatibility

This PR introduces a new architecture without modifying the behavior of existing Gemma4 models.

Existing Gemma4 checkpoints continue to function as before.

---

- [x] Added Quatfit1 model implementation

- [x] Registered AutoModel
- [x] Registered AutoModelForCausalLM
- [x] Registered AutoModelForImageTextToText
- [x] Added Quatfit1 configuration mappings
- [x] Verified model loading
- [x] Verified inference

items.title: [Model] Support `use_cache=False` for DeepSeek V4
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=46965)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=46965)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Purpose ##
* Support inferences with DSV4 without using kv cache

## Testing ##
Used these changes to calibrate and quantize https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4-FP8

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForCausalLM

def test_dsv4_cache_consistency():
    # Load the config from the pretrained model
    model_id = "inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V4-2.7B-tiny"
    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id)

    # Set device
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    print(f"Using device: {device}")

    # Create model from config with random weights
    print("Creating model from config with random weights...")
    with torch.device(device):
        model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    model.eval()

    # Create random input
    batch_size = 2
    seq_length = 10
    vocab_size = config.vocab_size
    input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (batch_size, seq_length)).to(device)

    print("Running inference with use_cache=True...")
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs_with_cache = model(
            input_ids=input_ids,
            use_cache=True,
        )

    print("Running inference with use_cache=False...")
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs_no_cache = model(
            input_ids=input_ids,
            use_cache=False,
        )

    assert not torch.all(outputs_with_cache.logits == 0)

    print("Comparing outputs...")
    # Compare the logits - they should be exactly the same
    torch.testing.assert_close(
        outputs_with_cache.logits,
        outputs_no_cache.logits,
        rtol=1e-3,
        atol=1e-3,
        msg="Outputs differ between use_cache=True and use_cache=False"
    )

    max_diff = torch.abs(outputs_with_cache.logits - outputs_no_cache.logits).max().item()
    print("✓ Test passed: Outputs are consistent between use_cache=True and use_cache=False")
    print(f"  Output shape: {outputs_with_cache.logits.shape}")
    print(f"  Max absolute difference: {max_diff:.2e}")
    print(f"  Mean of outputs: {outputs_with_cache.logits.mean().item():.2e}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_dsv4_cache_consistency()
```

items.title: [`peft`] Support key_mapping with PEFT models
items.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=46766)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=46766)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Hello!

# What does this PR do?

When a `key_mapping` is passed to `from_pretrained` for a model that also loads a PEFT adapter, the mapping was applied to the base model weights but silently **not** to the adapter (LoRA) weights. As a result, an adapter whose keys only line up with the model after the mapping is dropped on load, leaving the LoRA at its fresh/zero init, i.e. the model silently degrades to the untrained base.

This PR makes `load_adapter` reuse the conversion mapping that `from_pretrained` already computed (which includes the user `key_mapping`) instead of recomputing it from scratch.

## Details
`from_pretrained` builds the weight conversions once, including any user `key_mapping`, and stashes them on `load_config.weight_mapping`:

```python
# modeling_utils.py, PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained
weight_conversions = get_model_conversion_mapping(model, key_mapping, hf_quantizer)
load_config = LoadStateDictConfig(..., weight_mapping=weight_conversions, ...)
...
model.load_adapter(_adapter_model_path, ..., load_config=load_config, ...)
```

But `load_adapter` ignored `load_config.weight_mapping` and recomputed the mapping **without** the `key_mapping`:

## The fix

```python
# after
weight_conversions = load_config.weight_mapping or get_model_conversion_mapping(self)
```

`load_config.weight_mapping` already contains the model's built-in conversions plus the user `key_mapping` (and accounts for the quantizer), so the adapter weights now go through the same conversion the base weights did. The `or` fallback preserves behaviour for direct `model.load_adapter(...)` calls, where no `from_pretrained`-supplied mapping exists.

## Code Agent Policy

- [x] I confirm that this is not a pure code agent PR.

The original bug was spotted when I tried to integrate https://huggingface.co/vidore/colpali into Sentence Transformers using agents. This model was trained with `colpali-engine`, whose `ColPali` class wraps PaliGemma under an extra `model.` level. Loading the adapter onto a current PaliGemma backbone therefore needs `key_mapping={"^model\\.": ""}` to strip the wrapper. This works fine for a pure PaliGemma model (e.g. https://huggingface.co/vidore/colpali-v1.2-merged), but not for a PEFT Adapter on a PaliGemma model (e.g. https://huggingface.co/vidore/colpali) as the `key_mapping` is ignored. An Agent also helped write the test.

items.title: fix: adapt Whisper models to use self.loss_function with num_items_in_batch support
items.body:
## Summary

- Fixes gradient accumulation for Whisper by replacing the manual `CrossEntropyLoss` instantiation with `self.loss_function`, which supports the `num_items_in_batch` parameter introduced in #34191.
- Adds an explicit `num_items_in_batch` parameter to both `WhisperForConditionalGeneration.forward()` and `WhisperForCausalLM.forward()`.
- Sets `self.loss_type = "ForMaskedLM"` in both Whisper class `__init__` methods so the correct (no-shift) loss is used without touching the global `LOSS_MAPPING`.

## Changes

**`src/transformers/models/whisper/modeling_whisper.py`**

- `WhisperForConditionalGeneration.__init__`: sets `self.loss_type = "ForMaskedLM"`. Encoder-decoder models receive labels already aligned with decoder logits — no token shifting is needed.
- `WhisperForConditionalGeneration.forward()`: adds `num_items_in_batch` parameter; replaces manual `CrossEntropyLoss` block with `self.loss_function(...)`.
- `WhisperForCausalLM.__init__`: same `self.loss_type = "ForMaskedLM"` override, preserving the original no-shift behavior.
- `WhisperForCausalLM.forward()`: same treatment.

**`src/transformers/loss/loss_utils.py`**

- No global mapping changes — `LOSS_MAPPING["ForConditionalGeneration"]` remains `ForCausalLMLoss` to avoid affecting decoder-only models like `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` and `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration` that rely on label shifting.

## Behavior

- When `num_items_in_batch=None` (default): loss is identical to the previous `CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="mean")` call — no behavior change.
- When `num_items_in_batch` is provided by the Trainer: loss is normalized correctly across gradient accumulation steps, fixing the GA bug.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify loss is unchanged when `num_items_in_batch=None`
- [ ] Verify loss is correctly normalized when `num_items_in_batch` is supplied
- [ ] Run existing Whisper tests: `pytest tests/models/whisper/ -x`

Closes #36119
